thread:
hana: FYI ran a DR failover dry-run routing reads to acct-B eu-west-1 (MRK replica). saw ~1.8% decrypt failures for ciphertexts that were generated in us-east-1 primary. CloudTrail shows Decrypt calls to the replica ARN.

carol: ack, i saw those spikes in the app logs. error we get is `InvalidCiphertextException: Ciphertext not valid for this KMS key`. retries to primary succeed. no AccessDenied in CloudTrail.

ben: `InvalidCiphertext` usually means the replica couldn't associate the ciphertext with its key material or the encryptionContext mismatched. any chance we added an encryptionContext on encrypt?

alice: we do attach a small context in a couple places (e.g. `{purpose: 'session'}`) but most paths don't. code snippet:
```
const resp = await kms.generateDataKey({ KeyId: primaryArn, KeySpec: 'AES_256', EncryptionContext: { purpose: 'session' } }).promise();
await kms.decrypt({ CiphertextBlob: Buffer.from(resp.CiphertextBlob, 'base64'), EncryptionContext: { purpose: 'session' } }).promise();
```
If encryptionContext is omitted on decrypt it fails. also note SDKs serialize contexts differently across versions.

dave: another dimension: grants and grant tokens. grants don't replicate across accounts. if we relied on a grant in the primary for some callers, the replica won't have that grant. CloudTrail would show Decrypt, no AccessDenied but InvalidCiphertext can still surface. any use of grantToken?

emma: i grabbed CloudTrail for one failing request:
```
Encrypt: region=us-east-1, key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/AAAA
GenerateDataKey: region=us-east-1, key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/AAAA
Decrypt attempt: region=eu-west-1, key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:444455556666:key/BBBB, principal=service-role/read-runner@acct-B
Error: InvalidCiphertextException
```

ben: good capture. check whether the ciphertext includes a "KMS Key ID" prefix that references the MRK ID vs the replica. MRK ciphertexts include the MRK id but the replica must have the same MRK metadata. Also confirm there was no concurrent rotation: did anyone trigger MRK rekey or create a new KMS multi-region replica in the last 24h?

carol: we rotated the primary roughly 14h ago, but console showed replication complete. still, i can reproduce deterministically with a small loop and save the raw base64 blobs for failing cases. will attach.

alice: i ran a quick grep for EncryptionContext in the repo: two places in legacy ingestion service still pass `{ purpose: 'session' }` and one new lambda does not. mismatch could cause a small fraction of blobs to fail depending on code path used to encrypt. also found one dependency pinned to aws-sdk v2.513 where context ordering serialization bug was reported in 2.5xx series — possible.

dave: on the replica side i checked key policy and it looks fine (principal allowed for Decrypt). but grant checks: there are no grants on the replica for the specific role; primary used a grant that allowed short-lived access to a service role. that won't exist on the replica since grants aren't replicated across accounts.

hana: interesting — but CloudTrail didn't show AccessDenied. how would grant absence cause InvalidCiphertext instead of AccessDenied?

ben: two flows: 1) if decrypt request reaches replica, KMS checks whether the ciphertext's wrapping key ID matches the replica's MRK metadata and whether the caller is authorized. If authorization fails you'd expect AccessDenied. InvalidCiphertext can occur when the ciphertext blob version or key material id embedded in the blob doesn't map to the replica's active key material (e.g., in-flight rotation, or prior to replication completion, or blob produced by a different regional non-MRK CMK). In our case a mix of encryptionContext mismatch + occasional path that used non-MRK regional CMK could explain ~2% rate.

emma: i also captured two failing blobs and ran the decrypted attempt against primary and replica with verbose debug. primary decrypt succeeds immediately; replica returns InvalidCiphertext. the blob header shows KeyId: `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/AAAA` and MRK id `mrk-xxxx` embedded. so it should map.

alice: could be a serialization/encoding quirk. older sdk code did: `CiphertextBlob: resp.CiphertextBlob.toString()` vs Buffer usage and then base64 roundtrip. if some callers double-encode or strip padding it could corrupt a minority of blobs. grep for `.toString()` usages on ciphertext.

carol: i found one legacy uploader that does `const blob = Buffer.from(kmsResp.CiphertextBlob).toString('base64')` and stores that, however the reader decodes with `Buffer.from(stored, 'utf8')` in a different service that lives in eu-west-1. that will corrupt some blobs if stored/transferred incorrectly. that matches the low percentage.

ben: bingo. so root cause likely: inconsistent encoding between producer and consumer causing some ciphertexts to be malformed by the time replica sees them, which surfaces as InvalidCiphertext on replica but primary can succeed because the decrypt path back to primary may be more forgiving or receives original blob in retry path.

dave: mitigation options:
- fix producer/consumer encoding to use consistent base64 roundtrip (single canonical encoding).
- on read path in eu-west-1, if decrypt fails with InvalidCiphertext, automatically fall back to routing Decrypt to primary (us-east-1) for that read (costly but safe).
- avoid granting ephemeral grants for cross-account replica access; use explicit key policy principals in replica so Decrypt can be handled locally.

emma: action items:
- carol: attach repro artifacts and example base64 blobs (assigned)
- alice: push fix for the legacy uploader encoding bug and add unit tests to validate base64 decode/encode roundtrip (assigned)
- dave: evaluate adding an automatic decrypt-fallback route for InvalidCiphertext errors in our SDK wrapper (assigned)
- ben: verify SDK versions and put upgrade guidance in the repo PR (assigned)
- hana: run another DR dry-run after fixes and report numbers (assigned)

kms-bot: docs: KMS multi-Region keys overview https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/multi-region-keys-overview.html

carol: will post blobs in a follow-up message and mark as ready once uploaded to the secure bucket. thanks all :thumbsup:
